newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Chechens, Russia complete draft treaty on ties.
newsitem.headline: Chechens, Russia complete draft treaty on ties.

text.p: Russia's Security Council secretary and top Chechen separatist officials on Friday put the final touches to a draft treaty mapping out relations between Moscow and the breakaway region, Itar-Tass news agency said.

Ivan Rybkin and the Chechen officials met in Nazran, capital of the Caucasian region of Ingushetia that borders Chechnya, to discuss the deal aimed at regulating links between the two sides until elections scheduled for January 27.

Tass quoted Rybkin as saying the agreement was now ready for signing by Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and the head of the Chechen rebel government, Aslan Maskhadov. A date and place for the signing have still to be fixed.

The deal mainly covers economic reconstruction of the region and also includes guarantees for tens of thousands of Russians caught up in the 21 months of bloody fighting that ended with a peace accord signed on August 31.

Despite the progress of their talks, a permanent political settlement remains elusive, with the Chechen side insisting on full independence and Moscow trying to keep the region within the Russian Federation.
Moscow has mooted the idea of making Chechnya, which has oil resources and a strategic oil pipeline, a free economic zone.

In a further sign of the problems facing the peace process, Russia confined its troop to barracks earlier this week after unidentified Chechens took two of its policemen hostage and the bodies of four soldiers were found near the capital Grozny.
Hostage-taking is a common risk in the region, where the fighting, which killed tens of thousands of people, led to a total breakdown in law and order.
The incidents followed the death of 68 people -- many of them from the border troops -- in a blast in a block of flats in the southern Russian Dagestan region neighbouring Chechnya.

Rebel leaders in Chechnya have angrily denied suggestions that they were responsible for the blast. However, they said they could not rule out that go-it-alone separatist fighters were behind the explosion.
